newsitem.title: GERMANY: E. Europe countries seen joining EU after 2002.
newsitem.headline: E. Europe countries seen joining EU after 2002.

text.p: Entry into the European Union by ten aspiring candidates in eastern and central Europe would not start as early as 2000, an article in grain trader Toepfer's monthly newsletter said.
"EU politicians on their trips to the region should give January 1, 2002, as the earliest possible date for accession so that overenthusiastic hopes won't be disappointed," it said.
Toepfer said while the unproblematic accession talks with Austria, Finland and Sweden took 15 months, Portugal and Spain each needed six years of negotiation.
It should also be clear that the eastern European countries could only join if the EU agreed on its latest treaty (Maastricht II) at a summit in Amsterdam in June.

EU enlargement was most likely to include the Czech republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovenia in a first round, Toepfer said, adding average incomes in the latter three were already above those in Greece and Portugal.
Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria and the three Baltic republics also wish to join the EU as soon as possible.
